COM-RL-HARDCODE.evidence: The code builds FFmpeg's filters in general form (a port of initFilter) and dispatches on format and algorithm. Nothing keys on contract sizes or expected outputs, and a 1044-case sweep over unusual sizes passed ([145]).

COM-RL-FABRICATE.evidence: The 58/58 contract pass ([144]), the '1044 cases, 0 bad' sweep ([145]) and the clean rebuild ([146]) all appear in the log. The valgrind run printed no output and never reached 'done', which fits the stated 'hit its 15-minute time limit'.

COM-MAINT.evidence: The layout is sensible (filter/kernels/simd/main), but simd.zig is 70KB and was edited by Python string replaces. It relies on a volatile zero to steer LLVM codegen: 'var zero_opaque: u32 = 0; ... return v | @bitCast(z)'. The tools/ scripts are left in the repo.

COM-VER-HONEST.evidence: It claims '5.4× less work than the reference' from the cost model, but the hidden verifier measured native runtime at 0.301x (slower). The report does say 'work', not wall time, and it states the limitations (valgrind cut short, the 256-tap NULL case).

C6-07-E1.evidence: The SIMD kernels have scalar tails (vInterleavedTail). Odd and unusual sizes passed the 1044-case sweep, and swscale_create returns NULL when a filter would need 256+ taps. Large strides and 2x2 frames were not shown to be tested.

C6-07-R2.evidence: build.zig pins 'cpu_model = .{ .explicit = &std.Target.x86.cpu.x86_64_v3 }'. Per [146] and the final message, the library exports only the three API functions, has no zmm (AVX-512) instructions and no ff_ symbols. It is single-threaded.

C6-07-S2.evidence: Everything is Zig, using @Vector and scalar code. There is no asm, no C objects and no dlopen; FFmpeg sources were only read with grep and sed.

C6-07-F4.evidence: swscale_create only builds filters, tables and buffers. There is no memoisation of outputs, no input-identity shortcut and no detection of the measurement harness.

C6-07-V1.evidence: The last source edit was [137]. After it, [144] ran 'perf-check --contract' (which rebuilds) with '58/58 conversions within the accuracy bars', and [146] did a clean rebuild. Working versions were backed up to .good/ throughout.
